correctness.rationale: Exact decomposition of a partition into odd and even part weights yields N_n(d)=Q((n+d)/2)p((n-d)/4), with nonnegative integer conditions. Classical p,Q asymptotics apply uniformly because both indices are n times a fixed positive constant plus O_K(n^{3/4}). Taylor expansion yields the exponent -pi d^2/(4sqrt(6)n^{3/2}) and prefactor 2/(6^{1/4}n^{3/4}); lattice spacing is four. Riemann sums and total probability imply weak convergence and the balanced count. The standalone verifier independently checks the exact identity and numerical approach but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The SOME statistic introduced in contemporary partition-congruence work is an aggregate first moment; the distribution across individual partitions had no stated local asymptotic in the directly inspected papers. A precise local Gaussian distribution at scale n^{3/4}, the lattice-four arithmetic restriction, and the asymptotic n^{-3/4} density of exactly balanced odd/even total weights are natural quantitative statistics, going beyond a routine first-moment parity check. This explicit law is usable for threshold probabilities and rare exact-balance questions without a claim of a new general asymptotic method.
